The short answerA hernia happens when tissue pushes through a weak spot in the muscle wall. Many hernias are repaired with a planned outpatient surgery. Your surgeon will explain your options, including whether watching it is reasonable for now.
Consult firstNo surgery at the first visit
Often outpatientMany patients go home the same day
Recovery planWritten plan for your situation
Board certifiedSurgeon on every case

Who it suits

People with a bulge or discomfort in the groin or near the belly button, often noticed when lifting or coughing. Your surgeon confirms the diagnosis at your consult.

What to expect

You talk through your symptoms, your surgeon examines the area and explains your options. Like any surgery, hernia repair has risks, such as infection or the hernia coming back. Your surgeon will go over them with you.

Questions people ask

Can a hernia go away on its own?

Hernias do not heal on their own, but some small ones can be watched. Your surgeon will tell you what fits your case.

Is hernia repair done laparoscopically?

Sometimes. Your surgeon will explain which approach fits your hernia and health.

When can I go back to work?

It depends on the repair and your job. You will get a plan before surgery.
